sections.en:
1 πλησιφαεὶς ('near-shining') the codex has. κορόεσα τροχόεσα ('maidenly, wheeling') the codex has. χρυσαμπαξ ('golden-gleaming') the codex has. 3 I would prefer διχό-
μηνις ('divided by the month'). θειάνθεια ('divine flower') the codex has, cf. Maxim. 403. 4 Or πολυφεγγὴς ('many-shining')?, cf. Manetho 2, 347,
460. 6 κορυθέολος ('helmet-shaking') the codex has. Perhaps ὀλοόφρων ('destructive-minded'), cf. Orac. Sybill. 12, 263. 6-7 βροτολυγὸς ('mortal-destroying')
the codex has. 7 λογολαμπής ('word-shining') the codex has. χαλκεομήτρις ('brazen-wombed') the codex has. 8 πυρόης ('fiery') the codex has. βριθαιχμὴς ('heavy-speared') conjectured by
Kroll, χρυσαυγλήεις ('golden-radiant') (cf. αἰγλήεις ('radiant'), Manetho 4, 153) or χρυσαυγής ('golden-beaming')? Boll. Perhaps
εὐπόλεμος ('good at war'). 9 κυθέρια ('Cytherean') the codex has. ζευξήγαμος παφήη ('marriage-yoking Paphian'). 10 νησος βασίλεια ('island queen') the codex has.
10 θαλλασόη ('of the sea'). ἐρασίμη ('lovely') the codex has. 11 στίλβον ('gleaming') the codex has. χελυοξόως ('tortoise-carving') the codex has.

summary.headline: Epithets of the Gods and Planets
summary.text: Astrological epithets for the Moon (Selene), Zeus, Ares, Aphrodite, and Hermes, including their mythological identities and descriptive attributes. A note cites Dorotheus Sidonius’s seven epithets of the stars in Codex Marcianus 313 and discusses rare vocabulary preserved from lost astrological books.
